From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: 
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: QBR headcount gating — resource commitment checkpoint

Team —

Quick alignment before the QBR deck is finalized later this week. I attached the current QBR resource snapshot and one backfill req that Finance is flagging (req-2026-342). Main asks:

- Can we lock the two senior infra hires (Req 342 backfill + one growth infra IC) for Nov start?
- If not, which roles can we deprioritize or push to H1?
- Any exceptions to the hiring freeze we want to surface to Exec (and why)?

Context: product delivery has a hard dependency on infra availability for the upcoming Dedicated launch. If we lose the backfill we risk a ~6 week slip.

Attachments: req-2026-342_backfill.pdf (application/pdf); QBR-resource-snapshot-20261104.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks — please reply with one-line decisions so I can update the QBR slide.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
VP, Product Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: QBR headcount gating — resource commitment checkpoint

Jordan —

Thanks for the heads up. My quick take:

- Approve req-2026-342 backfill as an exception. Backend infra coverage is critical and the cost delta vs. the slip is larger.
- Defer the growth infra IC (non-blocker) to Jan recruiting slate.
- No other exceptions at this time.

I want Finance to confirm burn impact but operationally I'm green on the backfill. If TalentOps can speed interview slots we can keep the Nov start.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
